captain_shield.why: Backtest lesson applies directly: in 25/26 every round where we faded the highest-EO captain we lost points on net, because the fade only pays on the ~40% of weeks he blanks while it costs catastrophically on the ~15% he hauls 15+. Haaland is the season cum_pts leader (APEX locked captaincy rule), is nailed, and ~40% of the field still puts the armband on him even in a derby week. If he returns 13+ and you captained elsewhere you drop ~22 pts to the largest single bloc in an 18-man league — that alone is half your 48-pt deficit, in the wrong direction. The xpts model's 3.75 is fixture-weighted and systematically understates his ceiling; FDR 4 suppresses his projection but not his shot volume.
captain_shield.counterweight: This is the softest Haaland-captain week of the season so far — consensus metrics rank him 3rd (CRF 10) behind Joao Pedro (8) and Palmer (9), so his captain share is likely 40% rather than his usual 55-60%. That caps the damage of an alternative armband more than usual. But 'capped damage' is not 'positive EV' — hold the armband.

captain_shield.why: Second shield, and the more urgent one. If Pedro returns a double-digit haul from the bench, that is a pure, unforced rank loss against 13 of your 17 rivals.
